finding: Current private BF16 CUTLASS projection uses32x128x32 CTA forM1..32, padding proposal rows. Target scalar exactness does not require this private draft tile. A common weight-major kernel can reduce proposal padding while preserving batch/scalar cache identity.
mechanism: Native BF16 m16n8k16 FP32 MMA. CTA covers64 weight rows and8/16/32 token columns selected only by count<=8/16/32;4 output warp groups per8-token group,128/256/512 threads. Shared K128 two-buffer producer for canonical weights and inputs;16-byte cp.async copies. In-row eight-element XOR swizzle usingrow&7 prevents stride128 fragment bank aliasing. Each output carries FP32 accumulator through ascending K16, then BF16 RNE once. No splitK, quantization, sidecar or request allocation.
numerical_boundary: Private draft reduction may differ from CUTLASS v1. All counts1..32 use the same per-output K16 sequence, including initialization/full step/cache-only append. Require full draft hidden/K/V independent CPU FP64 max-row relativeL2<=0.02 without widening; complete target-state/full-logit/committed output must remain bitwise scalar target. Acceptance/work changes are allowed and explicitly reported, not compared as unchanged by assumption.
reference_transfer: Existing CUTLASS/Marlin separation of shared operand producer and Tensor Core consumer, translated to native SM87 cp.async and inline MMA. No imported source/runtime dependency, no cuBLAS production route.
